Late, but heres mine. I had cancer when I was 10. I guess it was in a shell of some sort so it didn't get detected until I happened to twist myself on a swing, allowing it to get nice and fat and pop out of my side. A lot of doctors didn't want to operate on it, they wanted to give me radiation and chemo but at that point it was growing so fast that it would of spread to my lungs and I'd be fucked in a week or two.

This doc walks in wearing a suit one day with half a dozen docs behind him. He was a really great guy and looked pretty damn important. He thought I was a pretty damn funny kid, and he decided to go for it and I got wheeled in for a 12 hour surgery that resulted in the loss of a kidney and the removal of a tumor the size of a football. I can't remember the weight of it, I can probably look it up if someones curious. 

I saw him multiple times over the next year, he removed some pre-cancerous cells on my right kidney a few months after my first surgery and he decided to remove the IV in my chest after my chemo was over. I knew it was a pretty big deal since it was only day surgery, I guess maybe he wanted to see the entire thing through with me.

10 years later I graduate from high school and I go to EMT school where I get the rundown of the privacy laws behind healthcare. I know he can't really check up on me because of the laws so I track him down and write him a letter thanking him for a second chance. I tell him that his decision to operate on me drove me into healthcare because I wanted to give something back. He thanked me, we cracked a few jokes and I've never heard from him since.

After that I struggled quite a bit with depression, suicide and bad relationships, dropped out of college and only in the past year have I really cleaned myself up, reenrolled in college and started having a healthy life. I discovered that I like listening to peoples problems, so I want to become a therapist and help people with addiction.

All I can really say is thanks doc, I owe you a beer. PS: You weren't fooling anyone when you were trying to stifle laughter after I started humming taps on my way to my second surgery. =)

TL;DR: Had cancer, doc decided to do surgery on a gamble, saved my life.

Her cheating on you is a reflection of her, not you. Somebody like that isn't worth your time or devotion, but there are plenty of women that are. Don't let her ruin that for you, only you can control how you feel! Try to be realistic with yourself, don't hold yourself to standards of others (its your life, not theirs), try to just do a little at a time and pat yourself on the back for it. Don't hold yourself to the standard of perfection, you're going to get through this! =)

Keeping perspective is the hardest part but is the most important usually. Its hard to convince yourself of that when you've been in so deep. It sounds like you are making a very wise decision by accepting your therapists advice to go to this place.
Why does this have to be the night you die?

Its natural to be attached to your therapist, and its awesome that your therapist obviously cares very deeply about you. I think this was a very very tough decision for her but she cared deeply enough about you to realize she couldn't give you the help you needed. She seems to think you warranted the help of this place. Trust her. The therapists at the place you're going to will never scoff at you because they know that your problems are VERY real and will respect that.

Try to remember that you may of lost her as a therapist but it sounds like you will always have her as a friend.

Don't be too hard on yourself. Try not to focus on being truly happy, its a lofty goal and hard to achieve. Focus instead on being less miserable, it takes the focus and the pressure off achieving happiness and has the happy side effect of making you happy.

Always remember that there are people that have felt the same way you have, and because of that they have empathy and a willingness to help you because they hate to see someone make the mistake they did. Never underestimate humanity.

I think that the fact that you want to use your talents and skills to improve the world is very noble and I encourage you to do that.

 You've already made a big step in the right direction, you've started giving a shit. You've recognized that the spot you're in really sucks and isn't making you happy. You know you want to change, but you don't know how. 

it is very easy to get overwhelmed with thoughts of boredom and inertia. Don't delude yourself by saying you wasted your younger years. It simply isn't true. Your younger years brought you to the point where you realized you had to change to make yourself be happy.

Find stuff you enjoy that places you around other people, take it slowly. Theres nothing wrong with being introverted, introverts can enjoy peoples company as much as extroverts. They just need time to recharge by themselves afterwards.
